transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Maud 3 FP, Hask 3 FP, Eira 3 FP, Fenwick 3 FP. Face-up: Endless Rain [H-01], The Blackwater Cartel [F-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the ford's rope bridge and the reed banks beyond it, the water already lapping at the third plank up. A line of miserable travelers shuffles toward a lantern-lit toll post where two Causeway Wardens check hands for hive-sores and pockets for coin, while somewhere under the planking you can hear the low creak of a Blackwater barge waiting its turn to be waved through with a different kind of toll. Maud recognizes faces in the line from Hollowmoot's congregation; Hask feels the current under the ford in his bones before he even sees it; Eira watches the Wardens' faces for one in particular; Fenwick keeps his hood low, mapping the safe pilings out of habit. The gate will close at full dark, toll paid or not.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Hold together and watch the deep run between those planks. I know this river, and I know how to get you across it.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud strides toward the familiar faces from Hollowmoot, her militia bearing evident despite disgrace. She reads the swollen water like scripture—the Ashwater Causeway taught her well—and positions herself among her congregation, shoulders squared and eyes tracking where the current cuts deepest between the planks.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The current's running strange — faster than the rain should push it alone. Something's stirring the water underneath.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask crouches at the ford's edge, fingers trailing through the cold water. He feels the current pulling against the pilings beneath the bridge with insistent pressure, his body reading patterns that only years on ferry lines could teach. His eyes narrow as he stands.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves quietly with the crowd toward the toll post, her gaze steady on the Wardens' faces, searching for Sella. She keeps her own hands in her coat and her hood up against the rain, unremarkable in the line.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: The ropework's failing on the western side—old maintenance at this ford. There's a path along the edge pilings if you know where the current runs weakest.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick keeps his hood drawn low and drifts with the shuffling line, but his eyes miss nothing. He watches the Wardens' pattern—which travelers they stop, which hands they grab, which pockets demand coin versus sores-checking—while beneath the bridge his gaze reads the rope's tension and the water's pressure on each piling. He traces an invisible map through the crowded planks, finding which route will bear weight without drawing attention.)

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Grandmother. You're not going to stand in that line like a target for slaughter. Come with me—I've walked the Ashwater Causeway and I've walked harder roads than this, and I didn't do it just to abandon my own when the water rises.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: No—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — overcome with Investigate: dice + 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Fenwick's eyes trace the pattern perfectly: he sees which planks bear weight, which Wardens are careless, and a slender gap along the western pilings that never sees a lantern's beam — a safe line across, if they move now. Maud, true to Hollowmoot's Faithful, breaks from the group to physically pull her grandmother from the toll line, guiding the shaking old woman past the crowd's edge — it costs precious minutes as the queue grumbles and a Warden's head turns toward the disturbance. Eira freezes mid-step: there, checking hands at the post, is Sella — the informer's face burned into her memory. Her composure cracks, just for a breath, and the flicker doesn't go unnoticed; one Warden's gaze lingers a beat too long on her before returning to his work. The rope bridge groans under the weight of the crowd, but Fenwick now has the map of safe passage in his mind, and the way is nearly clear.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: This way—the current cuts weakest at the western edge. I've walked the Ashwater and I know what this river's saying. Step where I step, and we'll be across before the light dies.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud plants herself between her grandmother and the Wardens' gaze, her shoulders squared like she's holding a shield-wall. Her eyes are on the water—reading it like scripture the way the Ashwater taught her—and she traces the line Fenwick found with absolute certainty in her posture. No hesitation, no fear; just the bearing of someone who's done harder things than this and means to do them again. She doesn't run. She doesn't skulk. She simply walks with such quiet command toward the western pilings that anyone watching might believe she has every right to be there, while guiding her shaking grandmother firmly but gently at her side. Her free hand is ready to catch anyone who stumbles.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The barge beneath us isn't sleeping anymore—something's stirred the Cartel to action, and we're about to be caught between two tolls.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask drops to a crouch at the water's edge and presses his palm flat against the ford, reading the current like language written in cold water. His fingers trace the pressure patterns beneath the bridge—every eddy and surge speaks its own truth. There: beneath the creaking planks, the massive bulk of the Blackwater barge is moving. Ropes sing taut. Crew active. The waiting is over.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I'm with you.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira allows Maud to guide her away from the toll post and the Wardens' attention. She keeps her head down and her eyes averted from Sella, moving quietly with the group toward the safer passage Fenwick has identified. She's trying to regain her composure and stop drawing notice from the lingering Warden's gaze.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: This way. Stay low, follow the west edge—the lanterns don't reach there.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick steps onto the western pilings, moving along the narrow safe path he's traced. He keeps to the shadows where the rope-light gaps exist, moving with the careful precision of someone who's read a thousand maps into his bones. He catches Maud's eye, then Eira's, with a gesture sharp as a compass needle—follow, now—before committing fully to the darkness along the edge.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — create advantage with Notice: dice - - + - → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The western pilings hold. One by one they cross — Fenwick leading with his silent, certain steps, Maud steering her grandmother's trembling weight through the dark with a shield-wall soldier's patience, Eira keeping her hood low and her breath even until the lantern-light is behind her. Beneath the planks the Blackwater barge finally breaks its mooring, ropes singing as its crew shove off into the current Hask read true — it slides past without slowing, without hailing them, its business tonight apparently elsewhere. They reach the far bank soaked, muddy, and unstopped, the toll gate's lantern shrinking behind them in the rain. But nothing is free at Gullet Ford: the Warden who marked Eira's flinch at Sella's face doesn't forget faces either, and somewhere behind you a coin has already changed hands to make sure of it.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: It's Jal, my cousin from the Gullet Ford ferry lines—we grew up together poling boats through those currents. When I recognize his hand on the spear, I don't hesitate. I throw myself forward to block it with my body.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Jal—cousin, is that you? I'm stopping this!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask refuses the compel on 'Born on the Ferry Lines'.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: When Captain Torvin betrayed the militia at Ashwater crossing, Maud was left broken and destitute in Hollowmoot. A Blackwater courier found her starving in an abandoned shrine and offered 20 silver to smuggle goods through the toll posts and watch for militia movements. She took the money with ashes in her mouth. She still owes them 8 silver—the rest has gone to keeping her grandmother alive through two harsh winters. To buy time, she swore them 'first knowledge' of any militia activity she learns of in the region, and promised to keep their contraband routes through Hollowmoot clear. The debt sits on her shoulders like the weight of every compromise.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: I've bought time with silver and shame already. Won't sell my people to the darkness. The line holds.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud refuses the compel on 'The Silver Debt'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: The pack that bursts from the flooded reeds isn't just feral strangers — Hask sees faces he knows in the ruin of them, hive-touched kin from the ferry-line he was born into at Gullet Ford, and they hook their spears through the current with the same waterman's grace his own family taught him. attacks at Gullet Ford using hooked spears thrust from the reed banks, because They come because Maud still owes coin to the Blackwater Cartel: the debt has gone unpaid too long, and someone in a night barge decided a hungry, hive-touched pack loosed at the ford is a cheaper collector than a knife in the dark..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The reeds explode outward as bodies crash through the shallows, hooked spears flashing in the grey light. Hask is already moving, throwing himself between Jal's spear-point and the rest of the party, cousin's name breaking in his throat even as Jal's ruined face shows no flicker of recognition — only the swarm-song's hunger. Maud plants herself at the rear, shield-wall instinct locking her feet in the mud, ashamed silver-debt or no, refusing to let the cartel's cheap collectors take anything more from her. The pack fans out along the western pilings and the drowned road beneath, driving straight for the party's packs and the dog-lead, everything dry and everything edible suddenly one wrong step from the black water.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Not today. I've already paid what I owed in shame—they get nothing more from me or mine. The line holds.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud plants her feet in the churning mud of the ford, shield raised into the high wall-stance she learned years ago marching the Ashwater Causeway with the Ashfield militia. Her shoulders lock, her breathing steadies into the old rhythm. She's a broken woman with a broken oath and a debt written in silver, but her *body* remembers how to be unbreakable—invoking "Never breaks a shield-wall" from the Oath of the Broken Line. She positions herself as an absolute barrier between the hive-touched and the party behind her, shield and presence alike refusing to yield an inch to the cartel's cheap collectors.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rill comes with me—you're my kin, but I'm standing fast here.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask plants himself squarely between the pack and Rill, drawing himself up to his full height. With the grace of someone who's spent his life reading currents and navigating treacherous waters, he moves to physically block any of the hive-touched from reaching the hound's lead. His jaw is set hard as he recognizes his own kin in their ruined faces.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I know these wards.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps closer, tracing old ward-signs in the air—the patterns taught behind the quarantine fence. Her fingers move between her companions and the pack, murmuring low sounds that once held sickness at bay.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: There—the western cut where the current runs deep. I've mapped every bend a dozen times over. Move through there now, and they cannot follow without losing the water entirely.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick's eyes dart across the roiling water with the precision of a mapmaker reading his own work—tracing the subtle currents, the reed-lines that mark deeper channels, the barely-submerged sandbars that only someone who's spent years charting this drowning country would see. His fingers point with absolute conviction to a slender cut between the pack's positions, where the drowned road forks deep and narrow, the kind of passage that swallows sound and breaks spear-formations.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — attack with Fight: dice + + 0 + → Fantastic (+6) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Jal and the Hive-Touched Pack taken out)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Athletics: dice - 0 - -, invoking Can pole a boat through any current [HA-01], Reads white water others cant [HA-04] → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — create advantage with Lore: dice - - 0 +, invoking Born in the Hollowmoot quarantine house [EI-01], Knows the old plague wards by heart [EI-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — create advantage with Lore: dice - - - -, invoking Knows every hidden channel between Hollowmoot and the reeds [FE-01] → Fair (+2) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud's shield-wall stance breaks Jal cleanly — a shoulder into the ruined shape of a man, and he folds into the shallows, spear skittering away, alive but stunned, the swarm-song's hold on him broken for now. Hask doesn't let go of Rill's lead for a second, planting himself as an unmovable wall between the hound and the rest of the pack even as his cousin goes down at Maud's feet; the others scatter rather than press an attack that's suddenly gone wrong. Eira's murmured ward-signs settle over the party like a held breath, the old quarantine patterns turning aside the worst of the pack's reach — Protected by Quarantine Wards holds true when it matters. Fenwick's western cut does the rest: he herds everyone into the narrow, deep-running channel he's mapped a dozen times, water swallowing their footsteps and breaking the pack's spear-line formation entirely, and within a few strides the shrieking and splashing behind them fades into rain and reed-hiss. When they finally stop to breathe, gear intact, Rill trembling but unbitten, Jal is a shrinking shape face-down in the shallows behind them — not dead, but not saved either, and Hask knows it.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Bren's eyes flash clear for one moment—genuinely clear—and he speaks their old warning signal from the hidden channel maps: 'North and dark.' Even as the swarm-song pulls his limbs forward, some core of Bren consciously throws his entire weight toward the Cartel enforcers instead of toward Fenwick, as if spending his last scrap of will to turn the blade away from his oldest friend rather than let the hive use him to kill him.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Bren, no—you're still fighting, I know you are! Hold on!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick accepts the compel on 'Bren, Lost to the Hive'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Hask is still shaking with the marsh fever caught days ago, and it brings feverish visions crawling up out of the water — for a heartbeat the reeds are full of shapes that aren't there, and he's already lashing out at one before anyone can stop him. turns on the party, because because the shape wading out of the flooded willows moves with a gait Fenwick would know anywhere — Bren, once his surveying partner, now hive-touched, calling his name in a voice half-drowned by the swarm-song. The bond holds Fenwick's hand still even as the moment costs the party everything..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The willows are still churning where Bren went down among the Cartel enforcers he threw himself at — 'North and dark,' still ringing in Fenwick's ears like a door slamming shut on hope. Hask is on his knees in the mud, fever-shakes wracking him, staring in horror at what his hands did in the delirium; Rill whines low against his side, refusing to leave. The enforcers who survived Bren's last act of will are not confused for long — hooked spears rise, and cold eyes count heads, weighing which of you is worth more as a hostage than a corpse. Somewhere behind them, the party's supply-pack — coin, maps, the safe route north — lies half-sunk and unguarded in the reeds.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Not him. You want something from this group, you come through me.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward through the mud and plants herself square between the enforcers and Hask's kneeling form. She doesn't draw her blade—doesn't need to. Her hand rests on the hilt with the quiet certainty of someone who's read a dozen liars and never flinched. The Hollowmoot faithful will follow her into fire; these enforcers can read that in her stance.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Follow me—the marsh knows us.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask forces himself upright, using Rill to steady himself as fever-delirium breaks like morning fog. His eyes find the dark water between the willows—the deep channels he learned on the ferry lines as a child. He moves low and certain toward that dark water, guiding the party where hooked spears become anchors and the marsh itself becomes their ally.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I'm good for what I owe the Cartel. We pass.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps forward slowly out of the shallows, moving with quiet purpose. Her hands are empty and visible, her hood still up. She approaches the enforcer boss with the same calm certainty she brings to any crisis—steady, unbothered by the spears.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: North! That passage runs deep through shadow—they can't follow with spears. Move, all of you, now!

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick's eyes snap to where Bren fell, then back to his companions—not a farewell but a map coordinate. 'North and dark.' His and Bren's own code from the channel surveys, burned through the hive-song by sheer force of will. He grabs Hask's shoulder, moving already, his eyes reading the reed-patterns and water-depths like pages in a book. There—the narrow throat of passage between the thickets, running deep where hooked spears cannot follow. He's heading into the dark on Bren's last gift.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Rapport: dice + + 0 - → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — create advantage with Stealth: dice 0 0 + +, invoking Knows the drowned roads beneath the water [HA-01] → Epic (+7) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Empathy: dice - + - 0, invoking Owes the Blackwater Cartel for smuggled medicine [EI-04], Can move unseen through smuggler tunnels [EI-04] → Epic (+7) vs Epic (+7): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick — overcome with Lore: dice + 0 0 + → Fantastic (+6) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Cartel Enforcer Boss attacks Hask (physical): Great (+4) vs Hask's Athletics Fair (+2) — hit for 2

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: You burned Three Elms on purpose. You all know it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira accepts the compel on 'The Massacre at Three Elms'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud doesn't move an inch, and something in that stillness breaks the enforcers' nerve — a heartbeat of hesitation that Hask reads like current on water, using it to haul himself past them into the dark channel he's known since before he could walk. Fenwick follows on Bren's last gift, 'north and dark' still burning behind his eyes, cutting a line through the reeds no spear can trace. But Eira's gambit curdles: 'You burned Three Elms on purpose,' she says, and the enforcer boss's face goes cold and flat — whatever chance there was of a bought passage dies right there, replaced by a debt collector's grudge with a face now. Steel flashes for Hask's leg as he scrambles up, fever-weak, and the hook bites — but it's a shallow, glancing wound, absorbed in the scramble, and then the willows swallow all four of them whole, the enforcers' shouts already fading into rain and reed-hiss behind. They've got the route. They've got each other. They do not, yet, have Bren.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The channel spits you out onto a low hummock of reed-root and drowned stone, barely wider than a cottage floor, but it's dry enough to kneel on. Rain still hisses through the willows, but here, for a moment, no spears, no barge-creak, no swarm-song — just the four of you, breathing. Hask shivers hard against Rill's flank, the fever's grip not yet broken, while Fenwick stares north into the dark like Bren's voice is still cutting a line through it. Maud checks hands and packs for what the crossing cost them; Eira watches the treeline, counting the seconds since anything last moved out there. The question isn't whether you rest — it's whether you can afford to, and what you'll owe by the time you're moving again.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: We hold here two hours and no longer. Eira, deep-well water if the reeds have it — boiled if we can risk the fire. Fenwick, north-facing watch. Hask, you stay down; fever needs cool and time, not another march.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud settles beside Hask with the weight of old habit, one hand finding his shoulder the way a shield-wall soldier touches the injured — steady, certain, no wasted movement. She reads his fever like water-sign, the heat coming off him all wrong, and her jaw tightens with recognition. The Pilgrim Road burned into her every memory of marsh-sickness: sweat that won't cool, breath that comes wrong, the sweet-sick smell of bad water settling in the blood. She looks across the hummock at the others — Fenwick staring north like Bren's voice is still cutting a line through the dark, Eira's hawk-eyes never leaving the treeline, Rill shaking against her master's leg — and something settles in her, the old steel coming back. Someone has to hold the line. Tonight it's her.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Bren's out there in the dark. But first I need to know what I did with these hands when the fever had me.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask stares at his trembling palms—something dark under the nails from things he did in the delirium that he can't remember and doesn't want to. He's still wracked with fever-shakes, pressed against Rill's steady flank for balance, eyes tracking the dark treeline to the north where Fenwick keeps staring like Bren's voice might still be cutting a line through the rain.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Hask, let me check your hands. The fever's getting worse.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira keeps her eyes on the dark treeline as she moves to Hask's side, kneeling to check his pulse and skin heat with steady, practiced hands.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I can't stay here. We move now, or I go alone. Bren's out there and the trail won't wait for us to rest.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick tears his gaze from the dark treeline and pushes himself upright, his hands already reaching for his pack with sharp, urgent movements. There's a desperation burning behind his eyes—the need to move, to follow, to not lose Bren a second time. His voice cuts through the rain-sound: 'North and dark. That's the channel to Saint Orrins, the drowned temple. Bren knew it. I know it.')

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: The trail is fresh. Bren went north—I know these channels better than anyone alive, and I won't sit here watching the rain drown the only lead we have. If the rest of you won't move, I'm going alone.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Fenwick's hand is already on his pack strap when Maud crosses the hummock in three strides and grips his wrist — not to stop him, but to make him look at her. "You go alone, you die alone, and Bren stays lost." It isn't kindness; it's the shield-wall soldier's math. Fenwick's jaw works, and the compel lands where it has to: the one surviving copy of the Order's false relic map is still tucked against his ribs, and just *having* it has made him a marked man since the day he took it. He can't leave it behind, and he can't stop reading it by feel in the dark, tracing the line that points away from Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple toward whatever Bren actually found. He accepts it — the weight of it, the fate point that comes with — and forces himself to crouch back down, map pressed flat under his palm, waiting. Eira gets her water boiled thin and bitter over a cupped, smothered flame, easing it past Hask's cracked lips while Rill presses close enough to shiver in time with him; the fever doesn't break, but it stops climbing, held level for now by Eira's steady hands and the plague-ward chants she learned before she had words for anything else. Two hours come and go with nothing louder than rain and Hask's ragged breathing — until, right at the edge of them, Fenwick swears he hears it: not the swarm-song, but boots. Careful ones. Someone out there knows how to move without splashing, and they're circling toward the hummock from the north — exactly the direction the map points.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Shelter at The stilt-house floor is laid over reed mats that hide beneath them the sucking black mire of the flooded lot — solid-looking ground that isn't ground at all. hides What the dry loft actually shelters is a feral hunting pack of the hive-touched, gone quiet and still in the dark above, waiting on the swarm-song..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The stilt-house rises out of the flood on tarred pilings, its door hanging loose on one hinge — an invitation the rain makes hard to refuse. Inside, the floor is laid with reed mats over what looks like solid boards, dry enough that for one aching moment it feels like salvation: a place to lay Hask down, to check Eira's wards against the fever, to let Fenwick's hands stop shaking around Bren's map. But the mats give a fraction under Maud's first step, a wet suck of black mud answering from beneath, and above your heads the loft has gone very, very quiet — the kind of quiet that isn't empty, just listening, waiting on a song only the hive-touched can hear.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The floor's a trap and something's waiting above. We hold the door. Stay close, stay sharp.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud's boot finds the weakness first — that treacherous give beneath the reed mat. She stops mid-stride, raises one hand sharply, and wheels back toward the threshold, her shield-wall training overriding everything else. "Back. The floor's rotten through." Her voice carries drill-yard authority, cutting through exhaustion and fever-blur. Her body moves into the blocking stance she's held a thousand times: weight forward, shoulders squared to fill the doorway, absolutely immovable. She's reading her companions' faces and bodies, gauging Hask's stability against his fever, Eira's strength, Fenwick's readiness — taking their measure and positioning herself to hold the line while her eyes track the loft's shadows.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Pack in the loft. Listening on the swarm-song—we move wrong, they drop.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask feels Rill stiffen against his leg, every muscle in the hound going rigid—that particular alertness that means swarm-touched presence above. His fever-clouded eyes snap upward, and years of marsh hunting flood back through the delirium. The loft's silence isn't empty. It's full of waiting bodies, the swarm-song thrumming like a held breath, and Hask reads the danger as clearly as current on water.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: The ground won't hold us. Back away slowly.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira steps carefully backward toward the door, hand raised to steady Hask, watching the barely-perceptible sag in the reed mats and the darkness of the loft above where something waits.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: The weight's all north in that loft—they're watching that way. The mire thins toward the west pilings. I can read us a path.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick moves with the steady precision of a man reading a map written in wood and water. His feet test each board before committing weight, while his eyes track the subtle sag of the structure above, the pressure-points that betray where the hive-touched are bunched. Despite the grief that has been drowning him since Bren went down, his hands are steady—the mapmaker's focus overriding everything else.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The four of you move as one now — Maud's raised hand freezing everyone mid-step, Hask's read of Rill's rigid spine confirming what waits above, Fenwick's eyes tracing the sag of old boards back to a dry seam along the western wall. No one breathes wrong. The loft stays silent, still listening for a mistake nobody makes. Fenwick's fingers find the line: a narrow run of pilings, firm underfoot, threading past the worst of the mire toward a gap in the back wall where the rain-noise alone will cover your retreat. You back out the way you came, Maud filling the doorway until the last of you clears it, and the stilt-house's false promise of shelter is left behind — trap and pack both undisturbed, and undisturbing.

violations.issue: Story cards MA-06 (event 13) and EI-06 (event 16) surfaced to the rail in scene 1 but were never returned to their owners' Story Piles at scene end ('At scene end, return it and its echo slips to its pile and reshuffle, unless it was retired'). No rail_remove event for either card appears anywhere in the log, including at scene 1's own cleanup (event 29) or any later scene end.

'The rail holds at most 5 face-up cards... If a card would exceed the limit, the GM removes the oldest non-GLOBAL GM card.' Because MA-06/EI-06 were never cleared (see above), the rail reached 6 cards at event 38 (H-01, F-01, MA-06, EI-06, HA-01, MA-04) with no discard logged, and reached at least 7 cards in scene 3 (after events 58, 59, 64) before only a single card (F-01) was discarded at event 66 — leaving the rail still over the 5-card cap.

'If the owner refuses, they pay 1 fate point. The GM builds the cost from a face-up GM tag instead.' Hask refused the HA-01 compel (event 34, pays 1 FP) and Maud refused the MA-04 compel (event 37, pays 1 FP), but no subsequent event shows a cost built from a face-up GM tag for either refusal — the scene's following rolls cite no GM tag tied to these refusals.
Same issue as above for the Maud/MA-04 refusal: no face-up GM tag cost is logged following the refusal.

ambiguities.detail: Arm definition lists Attention; not modelled.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Fate Core: boxes 1 and 2; Physique/Will +1/+2 adds a 3 box, +3 or more adds 3 and 4.

ambiguities.issue: Does a GLOBAL anchor give the GM a free invoke like a GM card?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Yes, GLOBAL cards placed on the rail give the GM 1 free invoke that scene.

ambiguities.issue: Success with style on create advantage: the aspect's 2 free invokes AND the deck peek, or one of them?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both: the aspect keeps 2 free invokes and the player may also peek.

ambiguities.issue: Does the session end after the climax scene?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Yes: the climax scene is the last scene of the session.
ambiguities.detail: deck exhausted in scene 5; climax = scene 6

ambiguities.issue: The rule only defines a fallback ('fills the first open blank still empty') for when a card's type matches NO open blank. It doesn't say what happens when a card's type DOES match an open blank, but that blank was already filled by another card drawn for the same frame (e.g. scene 3 BETRAYAL: HAZARD H-05, whose natural slot is HOW, fell through to WHO because BETRAYAL has no HOW blank open, which is fine — but then ROOTS FE-02, whose natural slot IS the open WHO blank, had to fall through to WHY because WHO was already taken by H-05; similarly scene 5 FALSE SANCTUARY: THREAT T-01 correctly filled HOW, then HAZARD H-04 — whose natural slot is also HOW — had to fall through to WHERE because HOW was already taken).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated 'natural slot already occupied' the same as 'type matches no open blank': the card fell through to the first still-empty blank in reading order. Result accepted as valid in both cases.

ambiguities.issue: Scenes 2 and 3 have no scene_test event logged at all, even though §7 step 1 says to run the scene test 'except in the session's first scene.' In both cases the scene instead opened directly with a Beat Frame/module deployed from the previous scene's cleanup trigger (B-01→scene 2's AMBUSH; M-2 and B-03→scene 3's BETRAYAL). The rules never state that a pre-deployed trigger replaces or skips the mandatory scene test.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated a cleanup-triggered Beat Frame/module deployment at the top of a scene as superseding that scene's scene test, running the frame instead and skipping the roll.

friction.text: Most deck-draw costs in this session (HA-01, MA-04, H-05, FE-02, EI-03) are flagged 'repaired:true' in the source data, meaning the first-pass narration didn't actually use the drawn tag and had to be rewritten to comply with §3's 'the cost must use the tag' rule — a recurring GM-side compliance gap.

The story cards MA-06 and EI-06 (drawn at events 13/16) were never returned to their Story Piles at any scene-end cleanup, leaving them permanently stuck on the rail; this silently ate 2 of the rail's 5 slots for the rest of the session and is the likely root cause of the repeated rail-overflow situations in scenes 2–3.

Scene 3 opened with two separate triggers firing simultaneously at cleanup (module M-2 and Beat Frame B-03), adding 4 cards to the rail in quick succession (C-01, T-03, H-05, then FE-02) with only a single reactive 'discard: rail limit' removal (F-01) in between — the cap of 5 was exceeded for several consecutive events rather than being maintained continuously as §7 implies.

free_text.best_moment: The enforcer standoff in S3 where Maud's shield-wall refusal to move broke the Cartel's nerve. It crystallized everything about her—the disgraced soldier who still holds the line, whose sheer integrity and unbreakability becomes her greatest strength. That moment *felt* earned.
free_text.most_frustrating: The stilt-house in S5 was too clean—we identified the trap, we solved it perfectly, and then just... left. No real consequence, no genuine confrontation with what waited above. It felt more like showing us a puzzle we could solve than like encountering actual danger.
free_text.background_used: Excellent integration. The Hollowmoot congregation (grandmother at the ford), the Ashwater training (reading water, shield-wall stances came up repeatedly), the Cartel debt creating the hive-touched pack with real moral weight—all of it woven in organically. Even Eira's Three Elms burn being weaponized against her felt like the world respecting established truth. The silver debt especially: I could refuse the compels and stay true to Maud's refusal to sell her people, but the debt kept creating consequences anyway. That's exactly how good compels work.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a real negotiation with the Cartel enforcers—a chance to use Maud's Rapport (her highest skill at +4) more actively to talk our way through or around a crisis rather than just escape. The enforcer moment was close but Eira's Three Elms revelation killed any chance to parley before I could try.
free_text.one_sentence: My backstory created meaningful moral weight and genuinely difficult choices—the compels were challenging without being unfair, and the silver debt made events feel personally stakes-heavy in exactly the right way.

free_text.best_moment: S2 — physically blocking Jal's spear with my body. That was a choice *I* made with real weight to it, recognizing my own kin and putting flesh between them and the party. Clear stakes, personal cost, no ambiguity.
free_text.most_frustrating: S3 — the fever delirium beat that made Hask lash out at allies. It was introduced as a GM complication, not something I steered into, and suddenly I'm managing guilt and consequences for an action I didn't consciously choose. Felt passive rather than active.
free_text.background_used: YES, heavily and well — the ferry lines (recognizing Jal's hand on the spear), reading currents like language, Rill's presence saving the party multiple times, the cost of knowing his own drowned kin. All of it landed naturally and created genuine stakes. The GM wove it in, not forced.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More active agency with the enforcer negotiation — I wanted Hask to use his personal knowledge (Blackwater debts, marsh connections) to maybe defuse or complicate the standoff, not just read danger and run. Also wanted more control over how the fever progressed rather than it being a bolt from GM complication.
free_text.one_sentence: My background was woven in skillfully and created real personal weight, but too many story complications felt imposed on me rather than driven by my choices — I was reactive more than proactive.

free_text.best_moment: Casting the quarantine ward signs in combat at Gullet Ford. Eira's hard-won knowledge from behind the quarantine fence became the crucial factor protecting the party—a moment where her quiet competence actually mattered most.
free_text.most_frustrating: Wanting to negotiate safely past the Cartel enforcer using my established connection to them, but the compel on 'The Massacre at Three Elms' forced me to accuse them of burning the settlement instead. Dramatically satisfying, tactically devastating.
free_text.background_used: Yes—Sella's appearance, the quarantine wards in combat, the Cartel connection, and the Three Elms massacre all appeared meaningfully. The GM wove personal elements effectively. Good.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Successfully negotiate past the Cartel enforcer using my existing connection before my character's need to accuse them of burning Three Elms forced the confrontation.
free_text.one_sentence: Eira's backstory was used well—personal elements created meaningful moments—though mostly through mechanical compels rather than through opportunities for her to seize initiative.

free_text.best_moment: S3 — Bren's clear eyes, the old channel code, and him throwing his weight at the enforcers instead of Fenwick. Perfect intersection of backstory, motivation, and heartbreak.
free_text.most_frustrating: S4 — being compelled to wait with the group after learning which direction Bren went. Mechanically earned but emotionally sting; Fenwick needed to move.
free_text.background_used: Bren card used excellently in S3 — felt earned and hit perfectly. Hidden channels knowledge is being used consistently but becoming predictable as a "solve navigation" tool. Enemy of Dry Saint and Cartel debt not yet engaged. Overall: good, but some cards underused.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Chase Bren immediately north after the "North and dark" signal; take genuine risks for what he wants rather than always finding the safe exit route.
free_text.one_sentence: My backstory with Bren was integrated beautifully and earned, but I'm narrowing into the role of "mapmaker who navigates around problems" instead of one who drives forward into stakes for personal reasons.
